title: Hyderabad Police Register Case Against Meta India Head Over Anti-Modi Facebook Videos
excerpt: The FIR escalates a rapidly deteriorating relationship between the Modi government and Meta, coming days after India summoned the company's executives over an inadvertent restriction on a prime ministerial Facebook post.
body:
• Hyderabad cyber crime police have registered a case against the head of Meta India over Facebook videos depicting PM Modi in an "abusive manner."
  • Police are preparing to serve notice on Meta Platforms but had not done so as of Friday.
  • The case follows India's IT ministry summoning Meta executives this week after Facebook briefly restricted a Modi post addressing student protests.
  • India is Facebook's biggest market by users, making the standoff particularly significant for Meta's global operations.

Police in Hyderabad have registered a criminal case against the head of Meta India over multiple videos posted on Facebook that depicted Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an "abusive manner," according to a senior police officer.

V Aravind Babu, deputy commissioner of police for cyber crimes in Hyderabad, told Reuters on Friday that police are preparing to send a formal notice to Meta Platforms regarding the case, though one had not yet been issued. Meta did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Escalating Tensions With Modi's Government

The FIR marks the latest and most direct legal action in a week of mounting friction between Meta and the Indian government. On Thursday, India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) summoned Meta executives after Facebook briefly restricted a video post by Modi last week — his first public address on the massive student protests that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign on July 26.

https://x.com/DDNewslive/status/2083055235707343025

"We have asked Meta to come in at the highest level and explain what is happening."

— S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

Meta said the post — which has since garnered more than 404 million views on Instagram — had been blocked "inadvertently." The company told Indian authorities it had established new protocols for accounts of prominent persons to prevent a recurrence. But government sources dismissed Meta's explanation as "not reasonable," with officials insisting that a technical glitch alone could not account for the removal of a post from the Prime Minister's official account.

The Student Protest Backdrop

The confrontation between Modi's government and Meta is unfolding against the backdrop of India's largest youth protests in decades. Triggered by leaked question papers for the NEET national medical entrance exam, the protests drew tens of thousands of students to the streets, culminating in marches on parliament in New Delhi that were met with tear gas and baton charges.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0qOEkLT_T1I

The self-styled Cockroach Janta Party spearheaded the movement, which succeeded in forcing Pradhan's resignation and extracting government commitments on exam reform, withdrawal of police cases against protesters, and compensation for families of students who died by suicide after the leaks. Modi has faced a barrage of online criticism, mockery, and memes from protesters throughout the unrest.

India's Supreme Court this week ordered the release of minors arrested during the demonstrations and directed authorities to preserve all surveillance footage, including from drones and body cameras, after petitioners alleged police brutality.

A Pattern of Big Tech Pressure

The FIR against Meta India's head follows a well-established Indian legal tactic in cybercrime investigations: naming a company's local chief as an accused to compel cooperation and information disclosure, rather than necessarily reflecting a finding of personal wrongdoing. Hyderabad's cyber crime police recently used the same approach in a separate case, naming Google India's head as a co-accused in a financial fraud investigation involving apps hosted on the Play Store.

The sparring with Meta is the latest instance of Modi's government confronting major technology companies over content moderation — a pattern that has intensified as social media became a primary battleground during the student protests. India, with its billion-plus users across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, is Meta's single largest market, giving New Delhi significant leverage in these disputes.

What Comes Next

The immediate question is whether Hyderabad police will formally serve notice on Meta and how the company will respond. With MeitY already demanding high-level explanations and the FIR adding criminal legal exposure, Meta faces pressure on multiple fronts in its most important market by user count. The outcome could set a precedent for how global technology platforms navigate content moderation disputes with the Indian government, particularly around politically sensitive material during periods of social unrest.
nri_angle: The standoff between India's government and Meta carries direct implications for how Indian diaspora communities use Facebook and Instagram to follow developments back home, particularly around politically sensitive content during periods of unrest.
